title: cone
body:
## cone

Creates a capped cone or frustum about the local Z axis with Blender's bmesh cone generator: radius at the lower (-Z) end, tipRadius at the upper (+Z) end and depth as the full height, centred on centre. A tipRadius of 0 gives a pointed cone; a positive tipRadius gives a frustum such as a nozzle or diffuser section.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- To point the tip downwards, rotate with transform (for example rotation [180, 0, 0]) rather than swapping radii.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `cone`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `radius` | Radius of the cone's base at the lower (-Z) end of its axis. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `1` |
| `tipRadius` | Radius of the upper (+Z) end. 0 closes the cone to a point; a positive value gives a frustum, and a value larger than radius widens the shape upwards. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0}` | `0` |
| `depth` | Full height of the cone along local Z; the base and tip sit at -depth/2 and +depth/2 relative to centre. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `2` |
| `segments` | Number of vertices around each end circle. More segments give a rounder silhouette and more faces; 3 gives a triangular pyramid. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `32` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the middle of the cone's axis (half-way between base and tip). Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated cone is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
